## Purpose
as described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39871, this is the first pr for it.
In this pr will
1. add marker pytest.mark.device_type
2. register this marker
3. using this decorator and refine the code under tests/v1
## Test Plan
CI
## Test Result
NA
## Limitation
This decorator can not work with the @create_new_process_for_each_test().
It is because vLLM's @create_new_process_for_each_test() forces the execution of the test function inside a completely separate, brand new OS subprocess to ensure CUDA runtime isolation, any process-specific Python state—including PyTorch’s active with torch.device(...) thread-local context wrapper—is completely erased when the new process boots up.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `device_type` pytest marker and an autouse fixture to manage the default PyTorch device context, enabling the removal of explicit device assignments across multiple test suites. Feedback highlights a potential `IndexError` in the fixture when arguments are missing and a significant issue regarding the thread-local nature of `torch.device`, which will likely cause failures in multi-threaded vLLM V1 tests. Furthermore, some test classes are missing the new marker, and several hardcoded device calls were missed during the refactoring.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Accessing `marker.args[0]` directly is unsafe as it will raise an `IndexError` if the marker is used without arguments (e.g., `@pytest.mark.device_type`). It is better to check for the existence of arguments or support keyword arguments for better robustness.

```python
        if not marker.args:
            yield
            return
        device = marker.args[0]
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `torch.device` context manager (available in PyTorch 2.4+) sets the default device for factory methods, but this setting is **thread-local**. 

In vLLM, background threads are frequently used (e.g., the engine loop in V1). Tensors created in those threads—such as those in fake sampler functions used in tests—will not inherit this default device and will fallback to CPU. This will cause device mismatch errors in tests that rely on background execution. Please consider the implications for multi-threaded test scenarios.

The class `TestCudagraphIntegration` is missing the `@pytest.mark.device_type(DEVICE_TYPE)` decorator. Without it, this refactored `SimpleMLP()` call and the `torch.zeros` at line 437 will default to CPU. Since the `CUDAGraphWrapper` expects CUDA-resident models and tensors, this will lead to device mismatch errors and test failures. Please ensure the marker is applied to the class or these specific methods.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Due to the missing `device_type` marker on the `TestCudagraphIntegration` class, `torch.randn(1, 10)` will default to CPU here, causing a mismatch with the model. Additionally, lines 492 and 497 still contain hardcoded `.to(DEVICE_TYPE)` calls which were missed in this refactoring pass and should be removed once the marker is applied.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `device_type` marker sets a thread-local default device. However, this test uses the vLLM V1 engine which executes in a background thread. The fake functions (e.g., `fake_sample_fn` at line 73 and `fake_propose_draft_token_ids_fn` at line 143) are called from that background thread and will now create CPU tensors because they no longer have explicit `device=DEVICE_TYPE` arguments. This will cause device mismatch crashes. You should likely revert the refactoring for tensors created inside these background-executed callbacks.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Accessing `marker.args[0]` directly is unsafe as it will raise an `IndexError` if the marker is used without arguments (e.g., `@pytest.mark.device_type`). It is better to check for the existence of arguments or support keyword arguments for better robustness.

```python
        if not marker.args:
            yield
            return
        device = marker.args[0]
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `torch.device` context manager (available in PyTorch 2.4+) sets the default device for factory methods, but this setting is **thread-local**. 

In vLLM, background threads are frequently used (e.g., the engine loop in V1). Tensors created in those threads—such as those in fake sampler functions used in tests—will not inherit this default device and will fallback to CPU. This will cause device mismatch errors in tests that rely on background execution. Please consider the implications for multi-threaded test scenarios.

The `device_type` marker sets a thread-local default device. However, this test uses the vLLM V1 engine which executes in a background thread. The fake functions (e.g., `fake_sample_fn` at line 73 and `fake_propose_draft_token_ids_fn` at line 143) are called from that background thread and will now create CPU tensors because they no longer have explicit `device=DEVICE_TYPE` arguments. This will cause device mismatch crashes. You should likely revert the refactoring for tensors created inside these background-executed callbacks.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `device_type` pytest marker and an autouse fixture to manage the default PyTorch device context, enabling the removal of explicit device assignments across multiple test suites. Feedback highlights a potential `IndexError` in the fixture when arguments are missing and a significant issue regarding the thread-local nature of `torch.device`, which will likely cause failures in multi-threaded vLLM V1 tests. Furthermore, some test classes are missing the new marker, and several hardcoded device calls were missed during the refactoring.

## Claude Code Review
